summary: This is a reference page for the BITMAP_COUNT aggregation function, which takes a bitmap representing the set of distinct values in a column and returns the number of distinct values whose bits are set. The page gives the syntax BITMAP_COUNT( <bitmap> ) and states that the argument must be a bitmap returned by a bitmap-building function, which is cut off in the note. Examples are not included and are referred to a separate guide on using bitmaps for hierarchical aggregations. Navigation and feedback boilerplate is omitted.
one_line: Reference page for the BITMAP_COUNT aggregation function, which returns the number of distinct values encoded in a bitmap.
key_facts: Given a bitmap that represents the set of distinct values for a column, BITMAP_COUNT returns the number of distinct values.
The single argument must evaluate to a bitmap returned by the bitmap-building function referenced in the note (name truncated in the source).
The function returns the number of distinct values in a column, as represented by the bits set in the input bitmap.
The page refers readers to 'Using Bitmaps to Compute Distinct Values for Hierarchical Aggregations' for examples.
The page is listed under the Bitwise, Hash and Count Distinct Values related function groups in its navigation.
